idea-plugin.name: SQL Dialect for DuckDB (embedded & Quack)
idea-plugin.description:
DuckDB SQL for DataGrip and IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate. A dedicated dialect and connection plugin for embedded database files, in-memory databases and remote Quack protocol v3 servers. This release targets DuckDB 2.0.0 and defaults new embedded data sources to DuckDB JDBC 2.0.0.0; JDBC 1.5.5.0 remains selectable.

DuckDB editing combines the plugin's dialect with the bundled Brikk SQL parser and scope analysis. Native syntax checking uses DuckDB's own parser through the parse-only json_serialize_sql function when a local DuckDB JDBC driver is available; it never prepares, binds or executes the authored statement. On matching file-backed connections, an isolated helper can reproduce registered custom PEG grammars such as psql for native validation and keyword completion.

Optional PIPE syntax is built in. After parameter substitution and before execution, the plugin transpiles pipelines into ordinary DuckDB SQL. The bundled Brikk translator rejects unsupported conversions and residual PIPE syntax. For statements supported by DuckDB's serializer, an available local JDBC driver provides an additional parse-only syntax check. Refused conversions and native parser rejections block submission. The generated statement, not the original pipeline, is sent for execution.

Compatible with the 2026.1 through 2026.3 IDE lines.

  • DuckDB editing: statement and run-block boundaries for SELECT * EXCLUDE(...), QUALIFY, GROUP BY ALL, struct/list literals, lambdas, PIVOT/UNPIVOT, FROM-first queries, ATTACH, SUMMARIZE and CREATE MACRO/SECRET. Historical parser evidence covers 226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5; this is not a full DuckDB 2.0 census.
  • Custom grammar profiles: manage registered PEG grammars in the data source's Grammars tab, separately from installed extension binaries. New registrations start enabled; disabled choices and activation order are remembered per project and source. Apply grammar changes updates idle sessions without reconnecting, losing temporary data or replaying scripts. Busy or transactional sessions retain pending changes until safe.
  • Native grammar-aware checking: isolated file-backed helpers apply and read back the exact managed grammar order before calling DuckDB's parse-only JSON serializer. Missing grammars, unmatched connection state and unsupported serialization produce no syntax verdict rather than a rejection from an unrelated base parser.
  • Native keyword completion: explicitly LOAD autocomplete on the connected source for engine keyword suggestions, including native psql pipe stages. This is independent of optional PIPE transpilation, and existing identifier/function completion stays available. Missing prerequisites appear in the Grammars tab, console status action and manual completion notifications.
  • Optional PIPE tools: enable under Settings > Tools > Database > DuckDB PIPE, write FROM t |> WHERE ... |> SELECT ..., preview generated SQL and run stages up to the caret. No SQL Transpiler plugin is required; ordinary FROM-first queries are unchanged, and remote execution does not require a local DuckDB driver.
  • Engine-aware completion and offline metadata: live functions come from duckdb_functions() on your connected engine and loaded extensions. Completion refreshes after INSTALL/LOAD; use Refresh DuckDB Catalog for autoloaded extensions. Offline metadata includes DuckDB 2.0 JSON/VARIANT and ICU functions, overloads, keywords and types, with extension hints and distinct window, aggregate, scalar and table-valued kinds. Builtin typing preserves scalar expressions and does not invent reader-output column layouts.
  • Database tree: browse tables, views, columns, keys and attached databases.
  • Ready-to-use connections: embedded and Quack templates download their drivers from Maven Central. Quack servers use jdbc:quack://, default port 9494, through Sortdev's Arrow-free quack-jdbc fork with protocol v3 support.

Native helper limits: file-backed native validation/completion requires a helper that can reproduce the selected profile. It is currently unavailable for in-memory, remote and follow-console modes, although those connections still support SQL execution. Native completion is keyword-only; injected SQL, unverified offsets, Unicode-space normalization cases and foreign attached catalogs are conservatively skipped. File suggestions are disabled. The plugin never silently installs or loads grammar/autocomplete modules, and does not disable signature checks.

IDE model scope: the updated shared Brikk SQL parser/scope model does not imply full native IDE PSI, typing or introspection coverage for every DuckDB 2.0 form. Recursive schema browsing, introspection and editing are not included in this release.

Remote Quack connection: put the token in the Password field and leave User blank. The IDE stores the token in its secure credential storage. TLS is off by default; add tls=true to the URL parameters for HTTPS endpoints.

GizmoSQL created the original quack-jdbc driver. The Sortdev fork used here adds protocol v3 support for DuckDB 2.0; the original driver does not support it.

Query cancellation: the preferred Quack JDBC 0.12.1 driver supports standard JDBC cancellation on Quack v3 servers. Existing sources may need their driver files upgraded; the older 0.8.0 driver silently ignores cancellation. JDBC statement query timeouts are not enforced by this driver; requestTimeout bounds individual HTTP requests.

This is an independent, community plugin developed by Sortdev SRL, not affiliated with DuckDB Labs, the DuckDB Foundation, or GizmoSQL. "DuckDB" is a trademark of the DuckDB Foundation, used only to identify the database this plugin supports. DuckDB logo used per the DuckDB design manual.

Source, issues and documentation: github.com/sort-dev/duckdb-intellij-plugin
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.6.1 - Live-catalog refresh ordering fixes with SQL IntelliJ support 0.4.1.
  • Aligns SQL IntelliJ common/JDBC/test support at 0.4.1. SQL/metadata/verifier 0.23.0, Quack JDBC 0.12.1 and DuckDB JDBC 2.0.0.0 are unchanged.
  • Prevents late catalog reads from restoring forgotten metadata or overwriting newer complete harvests. Failed, incomplete and cancelled reads do not displace the last complete catalog; queued work cannot restore a forgotten catalog.
  • Existing connection settings, grammar preferences and native-helper limitations are unchanged. Older 0.6.0 assets remain available and are not replaced.
0.6.0 - DuckDB 2.0 language, metadata and Quack driver updates.
  • Uses Brikk SQL/metadata/verifier 0.23.0 and SQL IntelliJ support/JDBC/test support 0.4.0 from Maven Central. DuckDB engine/JDBC remains 2.0.0/2.0.0.0.
  • Refreshes offline DuckDB 2.0 functions, overloads, keywords and types, including JSON/VARIANT and ICU functions. Preserves window-function and scalar/table-valued completion distinctions.
  • Updates the bundled Brikk SQL language model and scope analysis for UPDATE/MERGE, side-effecting CTEs, keyed recursion, NEAREST joins, VARIANT and newer COPY forms. This shared parser/scope/lowering support is not a claim of complete native IDE coverage or recursive schema browsing.
  • Updates builtin return-type handling while preserving scalar/relation separation, unknown-name diagnostics and real INSERT-layout errors. Unknown reader outputs are not guessed into table shapes.
  • Aligns parse-only checking with the 2.0 serializer; unsupported statements remain unverified. Native autocomplete verifies the reviewed extension origin/signature, and helpers reject stale console, connection/driver and module identities without reconnecting or replaying user scripts.
  • Prefers Quack JDBC 0.12.1, with standard Statement.cancel() support on Quack v3 servers and a bounded cancellation-control deadline. Unconfirmed cancellation closes the session rather than claiming success. Older driver versions remain selectable; existing source URLs, credentials and grammar profiles are unchanged.
  • Updates driver result classification so SELECT and RETURNING rows named Count or rows_affected remain result sets, while affected-row counts and end-of-results remain distinct.
  • Recursive IDE schema support remains deferred. Remote, memory and follow-console native grammar helper limitations are unchanged; authored SQL is never prepared or executed for editor checking, and mutations are not retried to recover results.
0.5.1 - Grammars tab compatibility with the IntelliJ 2026.3 EAP.
  • Implements the new native option-provider stored-default method to prevent AbstractMethodError on IU-263.7307.44. The host placeholder remains false; this method never saves grammar profiles or reconnects data sources.
  • Retains the 2026.1 compile baseline and 2026.1/2026.2 runtime support. Shared Brikk dependencies and grammar behavior are unchanged.
0.5.0 - DuckDB 2.0, custom SQL grammars and native keyword completion.
  • Default embedded JDBC driver 2.0.0.0, with 1.5.5.0 retained. Embedded file, in-memory and Quack v3 execution connectivity are supported.
  • Per-project/source Grammars tab with ordered activation, new registered grammars enabled by default, and remembered disabled choices. Explicit grammar Apply saves outside connection configuration and updates idle sessions without reconnecting; busy/transactional sessions defer safely.
  • Matching file-backed parse-only validation for custom PEG grammar plugins, tested with signed community psql. Missing state and unsupported serialization remain unavailable/unverified.
  • Native keyword/stage completion through explicitly loaded autocomplete, independent of Brikk PIPE. Preserves existing identifiers/functions, handles UTF-8 offsets and intraword insertion, and retains following SQL.
  • Visible missing-autocomplete and unsupported-memory diagnostics even when a lookup is empty; source-bound status action and helper lifecycle guards.
  • Native memory/remote/follow-console helper parity remains unavailable. No silent module installation/loading, authored-SQL execution for checking, or relaxed signature policy.
  • Uses the aligned Brikk SQL 0.20.1 and SQL IntelliJ support/JDBC adapter 0.2.4 release coordinates.
0.4.4 - platform API cleanup.
  • SQL IntelliJ support 0.2.3: no deprecated, scheduled-for-removal or experimental platform calls that have stable equivalents; no behavior changes.
0.4.3 - user-facing docs and SQL Transpiler scratches.
  • Engine errors for this dialect's blocks in SQL Transpiler .bsql scratches, and its completion and catalog features resolve against the block's own using= connection (SQL IntelliJ support 0.2.2).
  • A user-facing README; remote connections are described as Quack servers, with the Quack JDBC fork's ownership made clear.
0.4.2 - SQL IntelliJ support and JDBC adapter 0.2.1.
  • Package JDBC routing in its dedicated adapter and remove redundant compatibility forwarding.
  • Remove experimental markers from Brikk's shared public APIs.
  • Keep Quack JDBC 0.8.0, embedded driver defaults and existing editing behavior.
0.4.1 - builtin recognition and driver/settings fixes.
  • Uses formal brikk-sql 0.20.0, SQL IntelliJ support 0.2.0 and Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.3.0 dependencies.
  • Recognizes DuckDB builtin functions, named reader arguments and type-name aliases; preserves unknown-name and genuine INSERT-layout diagnostics.
  • Restores targeted automatic introspection after clearing metadata, including attached catalogs and schemas.
  • Fixes data-source picker icons and hides inapplicable PIPE menus. PIPE settings are under Tools > Database > DuckDB PIPE.
  • Updates Quack JDBC to 0.8.0. Remote query cancellation remains unsupported.
0.3.5 - dogfood build with formal Brikk releases and shared column completion.
  • Uses brikk-sql 0.19.1, SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.1 and Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.2.0 from Maven Central.
  • Shows brikk column types, nullability and source aliases using the shared renderer.
  • Keeps same-named join columns distinct without changing insertion text or SQL scope selection.
  • No Maven Local dependency or native database engine is bundled.
0.3.4 - shared SQL support backport.
  • Source builds now use formal brikk-sql 0.19.1 and Brikk Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.2.0.
  • Brikk SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.1 provides shared column presentation, including distinct suggestions for join aliases.
  • Maven Local and the temporary lexical guard are removed.
  • Earlier local testing ZIPs used brikk-sql 0.19.0-SNAPSHOT to validate the upstream unfinished-comment fix.
  • No native engine, verification library or compiler plugin is bundled.
0.3.3 - shared SQL IntelliJ support backport.
  • Uses Brikk SQL IntelliJ support 0.1.0 for cooperative Execute actions and translated scripts.
  • Uses brikk-sql 0.19.0 for statement boundaries and parser-backed parameter discovery.
  • Substitutes parameters before lowering, rejects stale preparation and keeps DuckDB validation policy.
0.3.2 - shared Brikk relation-contract support.
  • Uses the published Brikk Kotlin IntelliJ support 0.1.0 library from Maven Central.
  • Resolves, completes and navigates Kotlin relation-input columns with statement-local aliases, joins and stage scopes supported by DuckDB PIPE syntax.
  • Preserves partial/unavailable contract distinctions and labelled generated-column navigation fallbacks. Kotlin remains optional.
0.3.1 - automatic DuckDB Brikk editing in Kotlin K2.
  • Recognizes resolved Sql.duckdb calls inside @BrikkSql and enables PIPE editing for that host without changing project settings.
  • Scalar Kotlin interpolations become named SQL binds while preserving Kotlin references and rename. Relation slots and literal constants retain their roles.
  • Preserves trimmed/escaped source mappings and rejects unsupported interpolations. Kotlin is optional; ordinary SQL and Doris injections are unchanged.
0.3.0 - built-in, per-project PIPE support.
  • Bundles brikk-sql 0.18.0 for PIPE translation, with no native database engine.
  • Enable under Settings > Tools > DuckDB PIPE. Defaults off.
  • Preview generated SQL, run stages up to the caret, and execute mixed scripts with normal console parameter prompting. Unsafe translations are blocked.
  • Cooperative Execute wrappers preserve Doris and other dialect handlers.
0.2.0 — the injected-SQL language id is now DuckDBSQL (was DuckDBBrikk), so embedding DuckDB SQL in a host language (Kotlin/Java string injection, @Language) reads cleanly. If you had manually set a file's dialect, re-pick DuckDB (sort.dev) once; connected data sources are unaffected.
0.1.1 — polish.
  • Fixed the DuckDB icon rendering oversized in the data source / driver UI.
  • Clearer names: the dialect is DuckDB (sort.dev), and the data-source drivers are DuckDB Embedded (sort.dev) and DuckDB via Quack (sort.dev) — distinct from the stock generic DuckDB driver.
  • Refreshed README; Kotlin/build toolchain updated. No behavior changes.

0.1.0 — first public release.
  • DuckDB dialect with correct statement/run-block boundaries — coverage measured against DuckDB's own test suite (226/226 sampled syntax families at DuckDB 1.5.5).
  • Engine-exact error checking by a real DuckDB from your driver (EXPLAIN-based, never executes).
  • Live per-connection completion: functions/keywords harvested from the connected engine (version- and extension-exact), refreshed automatically when INSTALL/LOAD runs in a console, or on demand via Refresh DuckDB Catalog; bundled 943-function snapshot offline, with "requires <extension>" hints.
  • Object tree from DuckDB's JDBC metadata — ATTACHed databases appear as catalogs, on both drivers.
  • Ready-made data sources: local/embedded DuckDB and GizmoSQL (token-auth quack-jdbc, port 9494); pinned drivers auto-download from Maven Central.
  • Known issue: query cancel over GizmoSQL is a quack-driver no-op (local cancel works); driver fix tracked.
